title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC1RF_1RA0LD_0LC0RE_1LD---_0RC0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC1RF_1RA0LD_0LC0RE_1LD---_0RC0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a counter. Write the tape as gap words 0^g 1. At the sample points it is 0^∞ 1 1 1 C> 0 0 1 [0^g1 1] ... [0^gk 1], so a state is the list of gaps; most are 3, forming blocks. Read the separators 1 1 1, 1, 5 between blocks as digits 2, 1, 0: one round trip of the head is a ternary decrement (a 2 gives a 3 to the block before it, a 1 takes a 3 from the block after it, the zeros below become 2, the first block gains a 3). A second kind of digit (1 0 1, 2 1, 0) stops the borrow and drains the block after it; blocks that run out bring merges and a special return. Every rule is proved in Lean for all sizes, and the machine halts from blank tape iff this model reaches the gaps (0,0,0) or (4,0) (halts_iff_model, kernel-checked, assuming the model never meets a pattern it does not cover; since 12 November also halts_iff_hybrid, with nothing assumed, for the model completed by plain machine steps on the uncovered patterns). The model matches the machine at all 129,587 bounces to 2·1010 steps and runs about 1089 bounces without halting or getting stuck.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 118,944 cells have been visited and 35,562 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.19).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text:
The head sweeps over long runs of a repeated word, rewriting each copy, for any number n of copies and any surrounding tape. Examples:
  • L F> (0001)^n R → L (0111)^n F> R
  • L C> (0010)^n R → L (1110)^n C> R
  • L A> (0100)^n R → L (1101)^n A> R
  • L B> (1000)^n R → L (1011)^n B> R
Generated by py/rules.py (tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: One bounce rewrites the gap list
claims.text: For every gap list: C sweeps right over gaps 3 and 5, the pairs (0,1) and (2,3) and the run (0,0,3,3), stops at the first other pattern (ten kinds, e.g. 1, x → x+2, 2, 1 → 3, 0, 0, x+2 → 1, 0, x, x+7 → 1, 0, x+1), and returns in a normal or a special state that rewrites what it passed (a 5 becomes 1 1 1); at the left end a 3 or 1 1 1 is put in front. 29 symbolic pieces from py/counter.py (bbtools.symtm), inductions over the passed tokens by hand.

claims.title: The two halting patterns
claims.text: A sweep that reaches the gaps (0,0,0) or (4,0) ends with E reading 1: the machine halts.

claims.title: Halting from blank tape is exactly halting of the counter model
claims.text: Blank tape reaches the gap list [1,1,1,1,0] in 71 steps. If the model started there never meets a pattern it does not cover (stuck), the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the model reaches halt. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

claims.title: With nothing assumed: halting is halting of the hybrid model
claims.text: The gap counter has rules for the patterns that occur; on any other pattern it answers stuck. The hybrid model hstep is defined on every state: it makes a bounce of the gap counter where that is defined, and otherwise it continues with single steps of the machine itself, on the configuration written out cell by cell. Proved: each move of the hybrid model is a run of the machine of at least one step, its halt is a halting configuration, and therefore, in plain words, the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the hybrid run from the gap list [1,1,1,1,0] reaches halt (halts_iff_hybrid). Nothing is assumed. Also proved: as long as the gap counter is not stuck, the hybrid run is exactly the run of the gap counter (hrun_of_runM). What this does not give: any understanding of the uncovered patterns. After such a pattern the hybrid model simply is the machine. The theorem removes the hypothesis from the statement, not the question whether an uncovered pattern is ever reached.

claims.title: The gap counter is inside its rules for the first 200 bounces
claims.text: Lean's kernel evaluates 200 bounces of the gap counter from [1,1,1,1,0]: no halt, no uncovered pattern.

claims.title: ... and for the first 30,000 bounces
claims.text: The same evaluation by compiled code, 30,000 bounces: no halt, no uncovered pattern (so on this stretch the hybrid model is the gap counter).

claims.title: Why the rules were not simply completed
claims.text: Tried on 12 November. From every uncovered stop pattern with up to three leading gaps ≤ 9 (840 cases, with different continuations) the machine itself comes back in the normal or the special return mode, or halts; it never leaves in another way (py/model.py has the covered cases only; the experiment is a plain simulation). But the outcomes do not form a short table: some uncovered patterns behave like further passable tokens (for example the gaps 2, 2 are passed and become 3, 0, 3, and the sweep goes on), and a cell-by-cell search for a complete decision tree does not close at depth 16. A complete gap-level model would need a second layer of sweep rules. An invariant of the run that keeps it inside the covered patterns is not known either.

claims.title: The model is the machine's run, bounce by bounce
claims.text: c/gapdump.c reads the gap list off the real machine at every sample point; the model (py/model.py check) predicts every one of the 129,587 bounces up to 2·1010 steps. The flat transcription of the Lean definitions agrees with the fast run-length version on the first 2,979.

claims.title: No halt for about 10<sup>89</sup> bounces of the model
claims.text: py/model.py far applies whole stretches of the ternary counter at once (checked against single bounces for 3·107 bounces) and extrapolates periodic stretches linearly, re-running one period at the far end of each extrapolation (sound if the periods depend on the block sizes only through lower bounds, which is argued, not proved). In 870 seconds it ran about 1089 bounces with no halt and no uncovered pattern; the list of gaps grew to 371 run-length entries, the largest blocks to about 90 digits.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open. By halts_iff_hybrid (nothing assumed) it is the question whether the hybrid model halts; by halts_iff_model, as long as the gap counter stays inside its rules, it is the question whether the counter ever reaches the gaps (0,0,0) or (4,0). The counter is Collatz-like, as for the other base-3 counters; no halt and no uncovered pattern in about 1089 bounces.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine never seems to stop, and it is proved in Lean that it halts exactly when a simple ternary counter reaches one of two patterns. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the counter, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: Proved in Lean: halting from blank tape is halting of an explicit gap-counter model.
The model and the C simulator agree at every bounce to 2·10<sup>10</sup> steps.
No halt in the accelerated model.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A list of gaps
html:
Read the tape as words 0^g 1: a run of g zeros closed by a 1. Stop the machine whenever the head, in C, sits right of the three 1s at the left end and is about to sweep right. The tape is then 1 1 1 C> 0 0 1 followed by gap words, so the configuration is just the list of gaps. Most gaps are 3 (0001), forming long blocks 3^m. Consecutive samples from step 8,767:

3^3  5     3^34 1 1 1  3^5  1 1 1 1 0
3^4  1 1 1 3^35 1      3^5  1 1 1 1 0
3^6  1     3^35 1      3^5  1 1 1 1 0
3^7  5     3^34 1      3^5  1 1 1 1 0
3^8  1 1 1 3^34 5      3^4  1 1 1 1 0

sections.heading: One bounce, one decrement
html:
Between samples C sweeps right, carrying 0 0 1 along, over every gap 3 and every gap 5. At the first other gap it turns, changing one bit: 1, x becomes x+2, 2, 1 becomes 3, 0, 0, x+2 becomes 1, 0, x. Going back the head turns each 5 it passed into 1 1 1, and at the left end a new 3 goes in front.

Read the separators 1 1 1, 1 and 5 as digits 2, 1, 0. Then a bounce is a ternary decrement, least significant digit first: zeros below the first nonzero digit become 2, a 2 becomes 1 and pushes a 3 into the block before it, a 1 becomes 0 and takes a 3 from the block after it. In the samples above: 2 1 → 1 1 → 0 1 → 2 0. Seen at the right end of the tape, blocks lose 6, 18, 54, 162 copies per cycle counting from the end.

sections.heading: Slow digits, merges and the special return
html:
A second kind of digit, 1 0 1 → 2 1 → 0, never passes the borrow on: each cycle of three moves a 3 from the block after it to the block before it, so it lasts until that block runs out. When blocks run out, other patterns appear. The sweep also passes the pairs (0,1) and (2,3) and the run (0,0,3,3); going back over them the head may switch to a special state, which at the next merge or at the left end inserts 1 1 1 instead of a 3. At the right end of the list a few more stops extend the tape (2 → 5 1 0, 4 → 1 1 1 1 0, ...).

All of this is one function on lists, bounceM, and each of its cases is a Lean theorem about the machine for all block sizes. The model predicts every one of the 129,587 bounces of the first 2·1010 steps.

sections.heading: Two patterns
html: The machine halts (E reading 1) when a sweep reaches the gaps (0,0,0) or (4,0): proved, and with the model's other cases it gives halting from blank tape ⇔ the counter reaches one of these patterns (assuming it never meets a pattern the model does not cover). The accelerated model has run about 1089 bounces without either. As with the other base-3 counters among the holdouts, deciding it looks like a Collatz-type problem.

What is assumed. The rules of the gap counter cover every pattern that has occurred, not every pattern one can write down. The theorem halts_iff_model therefore says: if the counter never meets an uncovered pattern, the machine halts exactly when the counter reaches one of the two halting patterns. A second theorem, halts_iff_hybrid, assumes nothing: it completes the model by letting it fall back to plain machine steps on an uncovered pattern, and says that the machine halts exactly when this completed model halts. The fallback has never been used (no uncovered pattern in about 1089 bounces of the model; in Lean, none in the first 30,000).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.509). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.19).
After 109 steps the tape spans 118,944 cells (78,535 left of the start, 193 right), with a density of 1s of 0.299.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A ternary counter on the list of gaps between 1s. One bounce of the head is a base-3 decrement of the separators between blocks of gap 3; every rule is proved in Lean. Proved with no assumption: the machine halts from blank tape iff a hybrid model halts (the gap counter wherever its rules apply, plain machine steps on the patterns they do not cover, which have never occurred). Open.
family: ternary counter on a gap list (base 3)
